Ринок оренди перегрітий майже всюди. Але переплата - це майже завжди наслідок помилок. Розповідаємо, як їх уникати. 

1. Комісії агентів 

У багатьох країнах (Німеччина, Іспанія, Португалія) комісійні це 1-2 місяці оренди. Часто її платить орендодавець, а не ви. Перевіряйте, хто має платити комісію. Якщо ж агент нав’язує оплату - шукайте напряму (Idealista, OLX тощо). 

2. Депозити 

Норма - 1-2 місяці, але часто вимагають 3-4. Це спроба на вас заробити. Торгуйтесь або йдіть. 

3. «Хитрі» контракти 

Короткі договори (3–6 міс.) із підвищенням ціни.
Читайте кожен пункт, особливо умови перегляду ціни й штрафи «за все». 

4. Переплата за мегаполіси 

Оренда в столицях і невеликих містах різниться у 2-3 рази.

📌 Найголовніше: 

Житло без контракту й офіційної реєстрації - ви без прав!

"Швидше, бо перехоплять!":
- не платіть нічого до перегляду

# 1 - ++One Hour. That Is All You Need to Start++. : -

Hello my friends. Welcome back. I hope you are safe and doing well wherever you are reading this today. I want to talk about something very real and very practical today. Something that I personally think about a lot because I am building my own online income journey right now alongside you. Here is the honest truth that most people miss completely - You do not need eight hours a day to start earning online. You do not need to quit your job tomorrow or abandon your family responsibilities or sit in front of a screen all day, - You need exactly one focused intentional hour daily. That is it. One hour of consistent action repeated every single day adds up to 365 hours of real work by the end of one year and what's more is this 365 hours of focused online work done in the right direction on the right platforms can genuinely change your financial situation in ways that will surprise you. I have seen this happen. And today I want to give you the complete honest practical blueprint for making that one daily hour count.

![ " \"47de6a67e0d02f67d22fabb04df3f3a13bf2f5e2f6a5ae296b1abd65142c9b34.jpg\""](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTBvWbDmJPkgnAJ56zkUEWUymXMPBr6itVA8Nd8N8oq1q/47de6a67e0d02f67d22fabb04df3f3a13bf2f5e2f6a5ae296b1abd65142c9b34.jpg)

# 2 - The Niches That Actually Make Serious Money for Beginners : -

Before we talk about platforms and strategies I need to talk about niches. Because choosing the wrong niche is like digging a well in the wrong location. You can dig for years and find nothing. But choosing the right niche is like finding a natural clean water. The water is already there waiting for you. From everything I have researched and personally experienced, the niches that consistently make serious money for complete beginners are these - Personal finance and money management, - consistently attracts millions of desperate readers every single day because everyone has money problems and everyone wants solutions; Health wellness and mental health is another massive niche because people are suffering in record numbers right now and searching urgently for answers; Spirituality and faith based content is growing rapidly especially during these war times and global uncertainties when people are searching for meaning hope and peace; Artificial intelligence and technology tutorials is perhaps the fastest growing niche of 2026 because every single person on Earth is trying to understand what AI means for their job, their business and their future. Cryptocurrency and blockchain education remains strong because most people still do not understand it and good clear honest explanations earn real loyal audiences. And finally education specifically helping students with subjects like mathematics, physics and science is an evergreen niche that never goes out of demand no matter what else is happening in the world around us. Pick one of these. Just one. Master it. Then expand.


![ "1.jpg"](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWUZGitnJ2x79W8ETeq93yLYsBdsK3UZaqt8ptNnh8YeL/1.jpg)

3 -++** The Platforms That Will Actually Pay You : **++**-**

 Now let us talk about the real platforms. The ones that actually put money in your pocket or crypto in your wallet with just one hour of daily work. Publish0x is where I personally started, back in 2022, and where I still consistently post. It pays you in cryptocurrency tokens just for writing and for reading other people's content. Zero investment required, Zero technical knowledge needed, - just write honestly about what you know and the platform rewards you; Medium Partner Program pays you real money via Stripe direct to your bank account based on how much time paying members spend reading your articles, (based on what I have read and reasearched for, I still don't have medium partner program), Many writers earn between fifty and five hundred dollars, monthly on Medium with consistent daily writing. Substack allows you to build a free newsletter audience first and then convert your most loyal readers into paid subscribers who pay you monthly directly (I have seen people on Substack earning more like medium), Hive Blog and Read.cash pay you in cryptocurrencies - HIVE and Bitcoin Cash respectively, just for posting quality content consistently. For teaching specifically, Skillshare and Udemy allow you to create one simple course and earn passive royalties every month for years from that single hour of initial creation work. Fiverr and Upwork allow you to sell your writing, design, teaching or consulting services starting from just five dollars per gig and scaling up as your reputation grows, and YouTube despite feeling intimidating to beginners rewards consistent creators through the Partner Program once you reach 1000 subscribers and 4000 watch hours which is genuinely achievable within one year of one daily hour of consistent video creation.

![ "AI is hilarious"](https://cdn.publish0x.com/prod/fs/cachedimages/2340594248-941b1a6b4808de468f35046ecaf9ff704fc51dbdf71d69054e9a9882f0b0c097.webp)

## **4 -** ++**How to Actually Use Your One Hour Every Day**++ **: -**

This is the part that most online earning guides completely skip and I think it is the most important part of everything I am sharing today. Having the right platforms and the right niche means nothing if you do not have a clear simple structure for how you use your one daily hour. Because one hour of scattered unfocused activity produces almost nothing. But one hour of deliberate structured action produces compounding results that build on each other day after day. Here is how I personally think about structuring that one hour. The first fifteen minutes should always be writing or creating. Not planning, not researching, not scrolling, but creating, writing the next paragraph of your blog post, recording the next sixty seconds of your video, writing the next section of your newsletter. Creation first - Always. The next twenty minutes should be publishing and cross posting your content across your chosen platforms. One piece of content posted to Publish0x, Medium and Hive Blog simultaneously, takes only minutes and triples your potential earning reach instantly. The next fifteen minutes should be genuine, authentic, community engagement. Commenting thoughtfully on other people's content, responding to comments on your own content, building real relationships with your audience because relationships are what convert casual readers into loyal paying subscribers over time. And the final ten minutes should be learning something new relevant to your niche. Watch one short YouTube tutorial. Read one article from a successful creator in your space. Study one platform's newest features. Consistent daily learning compounds just as powerfully as consistent daily creating.

**Your Simple One Hour Daily Structure:**

- ✍️ **0 to 15 min** - Create. Write publish record or design something new without distraction.
- 📤 **15 to 35 min** - Publish and cross post across all your active platforms simultaneously.
- 🤝 **35 to 50 min** - Engage genuinely with your community and respond to every comment.
- 📚 **50 to 60 min** - Learn one new thing relevant to your niche or platform growth.

 

![ "0f51469f1d5a6cf5cf922a4fbb59cfa27bc6fba2cc8bec64cfc3082632af8d9d.jpg"](https://cdn.publish0x.com/prod/fs/cachedimages/884812937-0f51469f1d5a6cf5cf922a4fbb59cfa27bc6fba2cc8bec64cfc3082632af8d9d.webp)

## **5 -** ++**The Honest Reality of What to Expect**++ **: -**

I want to be completely real with you here because I think dishonesty about timelines is one of the biggest reasons people give up on online earning before their harvest arrives. In your first month you will probably earn almost nothing. Maybe a few cents on Publish0x. Maybe zero views on your first Medium article. Maybe one or two followers on your new Substack. And I need you to hear this clearly - that is completely normal, that is not failure, that is foundation building. The online creators who are earning thousands of dollars monthly today, all have embarrassing first months in their history that looked exactly like yours will look. By month three, with consistent daily one hour action, you should start seeing small, but real earnings. Between one and twenty dollars across your platforms depending on your niche consistency and content quality. By month six with continued consistency and smart cross posting those numbers should grow to between twenty and one hundred dollars monthly. By the end of your first full year of one daily hour consistently applied you should realistically be looking at somewhere between one hundred and five hundred dollars monthly depending on how well you chose your niche how consistently you showed up and how generously you served your growing audience. These are not extraordinary numbers. But they are real. They are honest. And they are the beginning of something that compounds far beyond year one if you simply do not quit before the harvest comes. Galatians 6:9 in Bible says that let us not become weary in doing good for at the proper time, we will reap a harvest if we do not give up. That verse was written two thousand years ago and it is still the most accurate description of building an online income that I have ever read.

----------------------------

It's been a long long time since I have been to Minnesota.  I remember when I was much younger, my parents decided to do the Lake Superior circle tour.  In case you aren't familiar with the concept, it's basically just a designated route around Lake Superior (called Gitche Gumee by the Ojibwa).  Each of the Great Lakes has a circle route (at least the three main ones that touch Michigan).  In the case of Superior, it takes you through the upper peninsula of Michigan into Wisconsin, then a short jaunt along the northern shore of the lake until you get into Canada.  Eventually, you find yourself back in Sault Ste. Marie and cross back over into Michigan making the circuit complete.

More recently, I had a flight layover in Minneapolis, but since we never left the airport, I don't really count that as having visited Minnesota.  This Summer, @mrsbozz and I are planning on taking a trip to Wisconsin.  It is very possible we will be making a quick drive over to Duluth to have lunch one day, so although it will be just a taste of the state, we should still be able to count having visited it on our map.


<center>![20230711_104853.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bozz/23rAtY8EB48skrEdqYXmNTsXSrkuUsnGYbFxTTtEADPDtsk58XwmnX8fwiyG7J2xiLd8R.jpg)</center>

--------------------------

Since I don't really have any photos of Minnesota, I am sharing photos of Lake Superior for this post.  In case you haven't guessed, this weeks #threetunetuesday sponsored by @ablaze brings us to the great state of Minnesota, land of 10,000 lakes.  When I was younger, I used to get annoyed that Minnesota was memorialized for its lakes.  I mean sure, it might have a lot of lakes, but we have the Great Lakes.  How much better is that?  It's funny the things you think are important when you are younger.

In fact, if you look at a map, Minnesota does indeed have a metric crap ton of lakes.  It's honestly no contest, but yes, Michigan still does have the Great Lakes.

Minnesota was actually a bit harder than I would have expected to find songs for this post.  Sure, it's not that easy to rhyme something with Minnesota, but I think we all know by now that not every song has to rhyme, it just makes it easier and a bit more catchy when it does.  

I was able to pick out three songs that I am going to share here, I hope you enjoy them.

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/KwbeHSI-3Co?si=kb4MEzqR_ivlmt12" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

--------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KwbeHSI-3Co&list=RDKwbeHSI-3Co&start_radio=1)

-------------------------

I know I might catch a lot of flack for this, but I am a huge Indigo Girls fan.  I understand there is this preconceived notion that only gay women like Indigo Girls music, but I think if you actually listen to them you will realize that isn't the case.  Or at least realize that shouldn't be the case.  The harmonies alone are so amazing, and then when you add in the lyrical prowess, there is just something really special about this duo.  

I was going to share a more recent video of the song "Ghost" from them, but honestly, these days their voices aren't quite the same as they used to be, so I found an older cut of it.  You just have to get past the overly long intro because it seems like the video is broken at first.  It isn't until about ten seconds in that you really start to hear it.

I really like the line in this song where they talk about the Mississippi River starting in Minnesota.  I've seen pictures of the headwaters of the Mississippi and to be honest, it's nothing special.  There is a little sign and then just a swampy area I think.  The part in the song where they say you can walk across it in five steps is just really poignant to me.

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/sNh-iw7gsuI?si=WMDbvDmHQsmaDpIp" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

---------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sNh-iw7gsuI&list=RDsNh-iw7gsuI&start_radio=1)

---------------------------

I'll be the first to admit, I never really got into Soundgarden when they were popular.  Yes, I knew the couple of big hits they had, but it wasn't until Chris Cornell passed away and it became more apparent just how many creative project he had his hands in and just how amazing he was.  "Outshined" has a reference to Minnesota if listen really closely.  I wouldn't have known it if I hadn't looked it up online, but I felt it would just be a little wrong to not include this prolific artist this week.

It doesn't take long to hear the reference to Minnesota.  It happens before we even get to the chorus in fact, but it is there.  If you watch the video with the captions on it is even easier to catch.  I don't have much else to say here.  Soundgarden kind of speaks for themself.

<center><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/bErza7LieSM?si=Xw3WUPfpIfvpKZ1A" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe></center>

---------------------------

[Direct Link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bErza7LieSM&list=RDbErza7LieSM&start_radio=1)

-------------------------

Finally, I realized it would be an absolute crime if I didn't include one of Minnesota's favorite sons in this post.  Of course I am talking about Prince and if you know, you know.  As I was preparing for this post yesterday, I realized just how little of his music I actually know.  Yes, I know the big hits, and the smaller ones too, but he had a massive career spanning back to the late 70's and an amazing catalog of music to sift through.

I've made it my mission to take a deep dive into his music on Spotify this week.  That doesn't even include the songs he wrote for so many other people.  

"Laydown" is one of the songs that I have probably never heard in my life until now and it's quite simple, but if you listen to the whole thing you will eventually hear the reference to Minnesota. It's too bad that Prince had to be taken from us so soon. I think he really could have made so much more great music.  

I remember maybe about twenty years ago he was in Michigan doing a show near where we lived.  I just kind of laughed it off and didn't have much interest in going to see him, but I really wish I had now.  Just to be able to say I saw a legend.

前幾次有提到，我最近開始上非常便宜的高爾夫球課，本來在練習場上課，但最後幾個禮拜到真的高爾夫球場上，然後又給我們開球車。平常租球車的錢就跟這堂課的錢差不多，所以這堂課等於免費了。

這次上課還是我第一次坐並駕駛高爾夫球車。這台球車其實比想像中聰明很多，速度不是想快就快，如果開得太快，它會自動幫你降速。上下坡的時候也很穩，幾乎不會讓人感到晃或不安，對第一次開的人來說真的很安心。前方還有一個螢幕，清楚顯示整個球場的地圖，現在在哪一洞、下一個目的地在哪裡，一眼就能看懂。

球具全部放在車後方，不用自己提著球桿袋在球場上走來走去，實在是太舒服了。想到上一次跟爸媽一起打高爾夫球，因為捨不得租車，幾乎整場都在走路，結束後累得不行，現在再回頭看，只能說下次再來一定會租車，完全不想再省那筆錢。

這次我和一位同學一起坐同一台球車，他以前有開過，所以一開始先簡單教了我怎麼操作，之後就讓我一路開到底。有個人坐在旁邊給點提示，心裡踏實很多，也很快就上手了。

打球的感覺也跟以前很不一樣。上次跟爸媽打的時候，幾乎還沒上過課，常常揮空，球也打不遠，現在因為已經上了一段時間的課，揮桿順多了。雖然談不上打得好，但至少每一顆球都打得到，而且大多都比之前更接近洞口，這種進步真的讓人很開心。

我們四個人一組，用的是那種選最遠落點再繼續打的方式，所以每一洞進行得非常快，不會卡關，也沒有壓力。大家邊玩邊笑，球很快就推進下一洞，整個過程流暢又輕鬆。

那天下課時，其實心裡有點捨不得離開球場。不只是因為開球車好玩，更因為真實地感覺到自己在慢慢進步。現在反而開始期待下一次上課，再一次把球車開上球道，繼續累積高爾夫回憶。

The African Harrier Hawk (Polyboroides typus) was previously known as a Gymnogene, which suited his athletic prowess as it is one of only a few bird species that can climb trees. 

*The two species of polyboroides (one in Africa and one in Madagascar) are large hawks with very broad, deeply slotted wings, long tails and long, slender legs which have the unique ability of being able to bend backwards and sideways at the tarsal (ankle) joint. This enables them to insert their feet into holes and cracks in rocks and tree stems to pull out bats, lizards, nestling birds, and other prey. Their unusually narrow small head also facilitates probing into holes. They have bare facial skin which changes color from red to yellow according to the bird's state of agitation.*     

Source: Book: Birds of Southern Africa. ISBN: 978-1-77584-668-0.

An image of me 

There was a time I couldn’t trust myself, not in a dramatic way tho but in small and quiet ways that slowly add up. I would promise myself I’d wake up early, then snooze and dismiss the alarm. I’d plan my day, then scroll it away. I’d say, “this time I’m serious,” but deep down, I didn’t even believe me anymore.

It’s a painful place to be as a woman when your words start to lose weight, even to yourself.

One evening, tired of starting over, I came across a video by Mel Robbins talking about something simple: the 5-second rule, not the one about food but about action.

She said, “If you have an instinct to act on a goal, you must move within 5 seconds before your brain kills it.”

I won’t lie, it sounded too simple, almost silly.

But the next morning, when my alarm rang, I felt that familiar urge to stay in bed. Normally, I would negotiate with myself, lose and sleep again.

But this time, I counted, 5… 4… 3… 2… 1…

I stood up like an armed force personnel resounding to orders 

Just like that, no motivation, no deep thinking, just movement and action 

This felt small but it felt different.

That same day, I used it again, when I wanted to procrastinate, i'd say 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 and start. When I felt like avoiding a difficult message, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, do it.

And slowly, something I didn’t expect happened, I started trusting myself again.

Not because I became perfect, but because I stopped overthinking myself out of action.

That’s what this lesson gave me: a way to interrupt fear, doubt, and delay.

As women, we carry so much in our minds, expectations, pressure, “what ifs,” fear of getting it wrong. And sometimes, it’s not that we don’t know what to do, we just don’t move.

That simple countdown became my bridge between knowing and doing.

And that’s why I would recommend learning from Mel Robbins to any woman who feels stuck in her own head.

Because it reminds you that confidence doesn’t come before action, it comes after action

You don’t need to feel ready, you don’t need to have it all figured out.

Sometimes, you just need 5 seconds and the courage to move before your fear speaks louder

Torch Myrmidon is a strong monster card in Splinterlands whose stats and abilities are very good. At the start I was thinking of it as a middle line monster and many times I used it in the middle line during battles. But now after getting more information actually it is a frontline monster.

If I talk about the identity of this card you can guess from its visual display. In the background you can see fire signs and in the top corner there is a fire symbol which proves that it belongs to the Fire splinter.

Its main role is a front line tank. It is known as a sustain fighter and its mana cost is eight. You can easily use it in mid to high mana battles while in low mana battles it can create some difficulty because its mana cost is high.

The most surprising and good thing about it is that even while being in the front line meaning while playing the role of a tank monster it can still attack. This is considered its special ability. 

![Screenshot 2026-04-21 101227.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/asgharali/23uQLi8GUHdd9hCBUxDeHZbtjPTQSsVfDMLdsuqhzK3LCKgJwFZeVbGgPJh2v1DFdVQCW.png)
![Capture.PNG](https://i.imgur.com/uGB0GKX.png)

For example if it is in the front line its armor which is 2 keeps giving it protection and along with that it keeps attacking with +1 every round. That means while staying in the front line it can keep attacking enemy monsters.

Its health is also good and its armor keeps trying to protect its health. Remember whenever you see high health and high armor in any monster card you can use them in the front line.

In the same way this monsters speed is 4 which helps in attacks. Torch Myrmidon has two special abilities that is Reach and Heal.

In Reach what happens is that it can attack from position 2. This means you can place it in position 2 and still attack. The benefit of this is that you can use a double front line. That means you can place one strong tank first and then place this card behind it and take full advantage of its abilities.

Its second ability is healing. That means in every round it restores a portion of its health and this is the strength of this card.

From its visual design I imagine that this monster looks very angry and because of its anger, flames are coming out from its head and a spear is passing above it. It looks like it is trying to damage enemy monsters. Its visual display is very beautiful and I tried to imagine and present this idea.

![Screenshot 2026-04-21 101155.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/asgharali/23tSN1PaLJLpZRR7fdeh383u7VSjkF3WYSsWJJZLtwHSjBGUkT3qA5mg5sqfjx6amxEg5.png)
![Capture.PNG](https://i.imgur.com/uGB0GKX.png)

Now lets talk about its weaknesses because every monster has its own weakness. Its first big weakness is that you cannot select it in low mana battles. Second it has only 1 melee attack so it will struggle against high health enemies. Third it can be affected by high burst damage meaning if the enemy has heavy damage it can make its heal ability useless.

Now if we talk about its price this monster is very strong but still very reasonable in price. In the screenshot you can see its minimum price is 0.087 which means at level 1 you can easily buy it and start your battles. Later if you want to upgrade it you can do that at each level which also impacts the price.

This was the summary of this powerful monster which I tried to explain in the best and simple way so that you can use such monsters correctly in battles.

# 10 Уникальных Советов по Оптимизации Производительности Linux для Вашего Серверного

Привет, администраторы! Если вы хотите, чтобы ваш сервер работал быстрее, чем вы успеваете выпить чашку кофе, вот 10 уникальных советов по оптимизации производительности Linux. И не забудьте, что даже самый быстрый сервер не спасет вас от медленного интернета!

## 1. Отключите ненужные службы
Зачем вашему серверу служба, которая отвечает за отправку факсов? Отключите все ненужные службы, чтобы освободить ресурсы. Помните, чем меньше служб, тем меньше шансов, что одна из них сломается и начнет петь песни о любви к старым версиям ядра.

## 2. Используйте SSD
Если ваш сервер все еще работает на HDD, то он как черепаха на марафоне. Пора перейти на SSD! Это как дать вашему серверу энергетик. Он будет работать быстрее, а вы сможете меньше нервничать.

## 3. Настройте SWAP
SWAP — это как запасной парашют. Вы надеетесь, что он вам не понадобится, но когда он нужен, лучше, чтобы он был настроен правильно. Убедитесь, что у вас достаточно SWAP, чтобы ваш сервер не упал, как старый компьютер на Windows 95.

## 4. Оптимизируйте конфигурацию ядра
Настройте ядро под ваши нужды. Это как выбрать идеальный размер футболки: слишком большая — не удобно, слишком малая — не дышит. Найдите баланс, и ваш сервер будет работать как часы.

## 5. Используйте кэширование
Кэширование — это как иметь запасную пиццу в холодильнике. Зачем ждать, когда можно просто достать ее и наслаждаться? Используйте кэширование для ускорения доступа к данным.

## 6. Мониторинг ресурсов
Следите за ресурсами вашего сервера, как за любимым питомцем. Если он начинает "пухнуть" (использовать много ресурсов), возможно, ему нужно немного меньше "лакомств" (процессов).

## 7. Настройка сетевых параметров
Оптимизируйте параметры сети, чтобы ваш сервер мог общаться быстрее, чем вы с коллегами за чашкой кофе. Настройте MTU и TCP, и наблюдайте, как скорость возрастает!

## 8. Удалите ненужные пакеты
Каждый ненужный пакет — это как лишний килограмм на весах. Удалите все, что не нужно, и пусть ваш сервер чувствует себя легче и быстрее. Не забывайте, что "чем меньше, тем лучше" работает и в мире серверов.

## 9. Используйте легковесные дистрибутивы
Если ваш сервер все еще использует тяжелый дистрибутив, возможно, ему стоит на диету. Легковесные дистрибутивы могут значительно улучшить производительность. Это как перейти с жирных бургеров на салат — сначала непривычно, но потом вы почувствуете себя лучше.

## 10. Регулярные обновления
Не забывайте обновлять систему и программное обеспечение. Это как регулярные медицинские осмотры для вашего сервера. Лучше предотвратить проблемы, чем потом пытаться их исправить, как после вечеринки с пивом и чипсами.

---

Надеюсь, эти советы помогут вам оптимизировать производительность вашего сервера до небес! Помните, что даже самый быстрый сервер не спасет вас от неполадок, если вы забудете сделать резервную копию! Удачи! 🚀

Wenn ich heute über Technik nachdenke, merke ich, wie schwer es geworden ist, ihren Anfang zu bestimmen. Sie ist einfach überall. Aber irgendwann muss es diesen ersten Moment gegeben haben, an dem ich ihr bewusst begegnet bin. Vielleicht war es das Telefon im Flur mit der Wählscheibe. Oder die Musiktruhe im Wohnzimmer – Plattenspieler und Radio in einem Möbelstück. Ich weiß es nicht mehr genau. Ich weiß nur: Diese Geräte gehörten nicht uns Kindern. Sie gehörten den Erwachsenen. Und genau dort beginnt meine persönliche Geschichte mit Technik. „Wenn ich versuche, mich zu erinnern, entsteht eine Art technologische Zeitlinie meines Lebens …“ ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/23u5QY15N5qMJKeX4xm6NEBhVJTciNWRBYRfVsDfQtvthhtkqviGsDBdgKjesHvFnTwz1.png)
Quelle: OpenAI Bildgenerator; @vanje ## Eine persönliche Zeitlinie ### Ende der 1960er – Technik gehört den Erwachsenen Erste bewusste Begegnungen mit Technik. Wählscheiben-Telefon im Flur. Musiktruhe im Wohnzimmer (Plattenspieler + Radio). ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/EqQPXhL6tvohCXKiJTEWbAELmzXdDH9RP4sWh8ASXhpYje63kZGDtCGtNE6USJUmBPE.png)
Quelle: OpenAI Bildgenerator; @vanje Schlager aus den 60ern. Technik ist teuer und fast ein „Heiligtum“. Kinder benutzen Geräte nicht – sie beobachten. Eine meiner stärksten Erinnerungen: Wenn das Telefon klingelte, war es oft mein Vater, der beruflich unterwegs war. Und mich wollte er immer sprechen. ### Frühe 1970er – Mein erstes eigenes Gerät Das erste Stück Technik, das wirklich mir gehörte: Ein kleines batteriebetriebenes Transistorradio, überall dabei, englischsprachige Musik entdecken (Abgrenzung zum Schlager der Erwachsenen). Technik wird zum ersten Mal Teil der eigenen Identität. ### Mitte / Ende der 1970er – Musik wird teilbar Der nächste große Schritt: Der Kassettenrekorder. Plötzlich konnte man: Musik aus dem Radio aufnehmen, eigene Kassetten erstellen, Musik mit Freunden tauschen. Das bedeutete aber auch: stundenlang auf einen Song warten. Aufnahme neu starten, wenn der Moderator hineinredet. ständig neue Batterien kaufen. Musik hören kostete damals Zeit und Energie. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/23wCLgCfALkgwY4UGpJo34aoaTo19FkHdJDcbvwFzCkS2yKLK6pUuwxyi3ZaWE3CSTrXv.png)
Image by MasterTux from Pixabay ### Ende der 1970er – Erste eigene HiFi-Anlage Weihnachtsgeschenk: eine Schneider Kompakt-Stereoanlage. Ich war ehrlich gesagt enttäuscht. Ich wollte: einzelne Komponenten, Geräte später austauschen, meine Anlage selbst zusammenstellen. Diese Enttäuschung führte zu etwas Neuem: Ich begann nach der Schule zu arbeiten, um Geld zu verdienen. Saisonarbeiten, Baujobs – oft half ich beim Vater eines Freundes, der Fliesenleger war. Der Bruder eines Freundes hatte sich mit Gerüstbau selbständig gemacht. ### 1985 – Der Heimcomputer Mit Beginn meines Studiums in Automatisierungstechnik kam der nächste große Sprung. Heimcomputer. Zur Auswahl standen damals: Commodore C64 und Schneider CPC ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/23xeVMaZpXJhwHrkHvAqD9pqJDXqRcedWnjAHbfViA4TX4MzFMQC9iED65ft7zBV75nLQ.png)
Quelle: OpenAI Bildgenerator; @vanje Unser Dozent riet uns: Wartet ein paar Wochen. Ihr werdet selbst merken, welcher Computer zu euch passt. Ich wartete natürlich nicht. Ein gutes Angebot führte schnell zum C64. Im Nachhinein war es eine gute Entscheidung – dort gab es viel mehr Möglichkeiten zu basteln und zu lernen. ### Ende der 1980er – Technik wird Beruf In der Ausbildung arbeiteten wir mit echten Mikroprozessoren: 8085, 8086, Z80 ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/23uEyoWVhoaXZhRCdob4cchTJgcMhC2R27y28dhJ27eoUtcnGwGf21WEcrBEuaGo9hr3V.png)
Quelle: OpenAI Bildgenerator; @vanje Programmiert wurde in: Assembler, BASIC, CP/M, SPS. Dazu kamen PID-Regler und Steuerungen. Software steuerte plötzlich reale Maschinen. Das war eine ganz andere Verantwortung als beim Heimcomputer. ### Automatisierung und Medizintechnik Mein erster beruflicher Einstieg: SPS-Programmierung. Entwickelte halbautomatische Prüfabläufe für Platinen. Später wechselte ich in die Medizintechnik. Entwicklung digitaler Systeme um wiederkehrende Abläufe zu automatisieren. Der PC wurde dabei mein ständiger Begleiter. Von PC-DOS, MS-DOS, bis zu Windows und später auch Linux. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/23wWvpez2MtaN83h61iRpsr3tukJGmxsy92qj9a2TBy69fDAM4Di5nvX3FBDGr3unBH1N.png)
Quelle: OpenAI Bildgenerator; @vanje ### Netzwerke und Infrastruktur Ein weiterer Schwerpunkt wurde Netzwerktechnik. Ich installierte Netzwerke bei: Freunden, kleinen Firmen, Selbstständigen. Damals meist 10-Mbit Ethernet. Fehlersuche war oft ein Albtraum. Ein defektes Kabel oder unsaubere Verbindung – und das ganze Netz stand. ### Vor dem Internet – BTX Noch bevor das Internet alltäglich wurde, arbeitete ich mit BTX (Bildschirmtext). Mit Freunden, einer hatte von seinem Vater einen größeren Kurierdienst übernommen, entwickelten wir eine interaktive Plattform zur Reduktion von Leerfahrten (OMS-2000). Technik dafür: GPS, D2 Mobilfunk, zentrale Plattform. Im Grunde ein früher Vorläufer moderner Logistikplattformen. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/23ynZ2z5hrGUkmYcxjeAzUhwGqu3RWxwgNnssVKLEjLHjnrK9J4UiWxxdDbcGGsgraXLN.png)
Vieles davon wirkt heute selbstverständlich. Damals (1990-1995) war es ein gefördertes Experiment. ### Frühe Online-Zeit – Modems und ISDN Die ersten Verbindungen ins Netz: Akustikkoppler (0,3k), 2.8k Modems, später 56k. Der große Fortschritt kam mit ISDN (64k), mit geeigneter teurer Hardware (aktive ISDN-Karte AVM B1) konnte man zwei Leitungen bündeln (128k). Jetzt konnte man stabil online arbeiten. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/23y9AZa9mm191utkVTvFTWCRQL5JhCtba4JhbtcFNK6KaDZHwYmvdUnGMed2MeC5TYKeG.png)
Quelle: OpenAI Bildgenerator; @vanje Ich begann Webseiten zu erstellen: für Freunde, für Vereine, für Selbstständige inklusive Infrastrukturplanung. Solange Technik eine Herausforderung war, machte sie besonders viel Spaß. ### Mobile Kommunikation Durch meinen Beruf war Erreichbarkeit wichtig. Ich begann mit dem B-Netz. Später kam mein erstes richtig mobiles Telefon - Ein Motorola-Klapphandy mit ausziehbarer Antenne. Erstaunlich gute Funkqualität für diese Zeit. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/23wqi9JZVFb8tMzfGrQNsnikgCdwNJ8xS3AjSFnGsgoym4ZYAhSSXkcfBDmDWvsXXpAcC.png)
Quelle: OpenAI Bildgenerator; @vanje ### Frühe Smartphones Noch lange bevor Apple oder Samsung den Markt dominierten, hatte ich bereits ein frühes Smartphone. Damit konnte man: E-Mails schreiben, Fotos machen, Termine verwalten. Damals fühlte sich das schon wie Zukunft an. ### Heute – Technik als Werkzeug Heute nutze ich Technik anders. Nicht mehr primär beruflich, sondern als Werkzeug für Gedanken, Austausch und Dokumentation. Zum Beispiel: Schreiben, Reflektieren, Publizieren. Technik unterstützt den Prozess – sie steht nicht mehr im Mittelpunkt. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vanje/23x1WXw2cyeXLjY5eizrASwWugaqNGbJ4n5aqwsHx9iAZt35oVUXUUMQXcNZB5o3GHRai.png)
Quelle: OpenAI Bildgenerator; @vanje ## Die eigentliche Entwicklung Wenn ich zurückblicke, sehe ich eine interessante Bewegung: - Technik war zuerst selten und zentral - Dann wurde sie persönlich - Später Werkzeug - Dann Infrastruktur - Und heute ist sie einfach Begleiter im Alltag. ## Schlussgedanke Wenn ich heute darüber nachdenke, habe ich eine erstaunliche Entwicklung miterlebt. - Von der Musiktruhe im Wohnzimmer zum Smartphone in der Hosentasche. - Von der Wählscheibe zu globalen Netzwerken. - Von Kassettenaufnahmen aus dem Radio zu Musikbibliotheken, die in Sekunden verfügbar sind. - Und vom Heimcomputer, auf dem man Programme noch aus Zeitschriften abtippte, hin zu Systemen, die heute mit Hilfe künstlicher Intelligenz Texte formulieren – und ganze Prozesse im Hintergrund mitdenken. Technik hat sich ständig verändert. Was sich dabei aber kaum verändert hat, ist etwas anderes: die Neugier. Der Wunsch zu verstehen, wie Dinge funktionieren. Probleme zu lösen. Neue Möglichkeiten auszuprobieren. Früher bedeutete das: Kassetten aufnehmen. Computer programmieren. Netzwerke aufbauen. Heute bedeutet es vielleicht: Gedanken aufschreiben. Erfahrungen teilen. Oder einfach beobachten, wohin sich diese technische Welt noch entwickelt. Wenn ich eines gelernt habe, dann: Technik kommt und geht. Aber die Neugier darauf bleibt.
